Definition: from G3844 and G5426; to misthink, i.e. be insane (silly):--as a fool.
BiblicalUsage: Paraphroneo means to be beside oneself, to speak as a fool. Paul uses it once, in 2 Corinthians 11:23, when he boasts of his sufferings and then catches himself: I speak as a fool, I am more.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul knew how foolish boasting sounds, and he did it anyway because the truth about his sufferings was worth the cost.
